slopsquatting-hallucinated-packages-supp.title: Slopsquatting and Hallucinated Packages: Supply-Chain Risk in AI-Written Code
slopsquatting-hallucinated-packages-supp.description: Code assistants sometimes import packages that do not exist, and attackers can register those names. What the research measured, why it is not just typosquatting, and the controls that close the gap.

the-rise-of-specialized-small-language-m.title: The Rise of Specialized Small Language Models (SLMs)
the-rise-of-specialized-small-language-m.description: Why the industry is moving away from massive models toward efficient, task-specific SLMs.

ai-adoption-small-engineering-teams-90-d.title: AI Adoption for Small Engineering Teams: A 90-Day Plan
ai-adoption-small-engineering-teams-90-d.description: Buying seats is not adoption. A three-phase plan for small teams to roll out AI coding tools with a baseline, guardrails and a decision at day 90, grounded in DORA and METR research.

spec-driven-development-writing-for-agen.title: Spec-Driven Development: Writing for Agents Before Writing Code
spec-driven-development-writing-for-agen.description: Spec Kit, Kiro and similar tools put a written specification in front of every coding agent run. What a useful spec contains, how the workflow runs, and when it is more ceremony than it is worth.

how-speculative-decoding-works-faster-ll.title: How Speculative Decoding Works: Big-Model Answers at Small-Model Speed
how-speculative-decoding-works-faster-ll.description: A small model guesses, a big model checks several guesses in one pass, and the output distribution does not change. How speculative decoding works, and when it stops helping.

how-state-space-models-work-mamba.title: How State Space Models Work: Mamba and Life Beyond Attention
how-state-space-models-work-mamba.description: A fixed-size state instead of a growing KV cache: how SSMs and Mamba's selection mechanism work, where they fall short, and why production models now mix them with attention.

structured-outputs-function-calling-mach.title: Structured Outputs and Function Calling: Making LLM Output Machine-Safe
structured-outputs-function-calling-mach.description: JSON mode, strict structured outputs and function calling explained: what constrained decoding guarantees, where each provider's schema limits bite, and the validation you still need in code.

swe-bench-is-solved-what-comes-next.title: SWE-bench Is Solved. So Why Do Coding Agents Still Break Your Repo?
swe-bench-is-solved-what-comes-next.description: Scores above 95% on the benchmark that defined the field, and OpenAI publicly declaring it dead. The gap between passing a test and doing the job.

synthetic-data-where-it-works-where-it-c.title: Synthetic Data: Where It Works, Where It Collapses
synthetic-data-where-it-works-where-it-c.description: Model-generated training data built instruction tuning, small code models and olympiad geometry. It also causes model collapse. The difference comes down to verification and whether real data stays in the mix.

testing-non-deterministic-ai-features.title: Testing Non-Deterministic Features: A Practical Strategy for AI Products
testing-non-deterministic-ai-features.description: Assertions on exact strings break the moment a model is involved. How to split deterministic from probabilistic, grade outputs you cannot predict, and gate releases on numbers you can trust.

how-tokenizers-work-bpe-vocabularies.title: How Tokenizers Work: BPE, Vocabularies and Why Models Can't Count Letters
how-tokenizers-work-bpe-vocabularies.description: Byte pair encoding, vocabulary size, byte-level fallback and the strange failures that come from a model never seeing letters. Explained with real token splits.

designing-tools-apis-agents-can-use.title: Designing Tools and APIs That Agents Can Actually Use
designing-tools-apis-agents-can-use.description: Agents read your tool descriptions on every call, never ask clarifying questions and pay for every token you return. How to design names, schemas, responses and errors for that kind of consumer.

typesafe-ai-jev-a-system-one-model-that-.title: TypeSafe AI Jev: A System One Model That Returns Decisions, Not Text
typesafe-ai-jev-a-system-one-model-that-.description: TypeSafe AI's Jev returns typed choices, scores and yes/no probabilities with confidence instead of text, at $0.042 per million input tokens.

how-vector-search-works-hnsw-recall.title: How Vector Search Works: Embeddings, HNSW and the Recall Trade-off
how-vector-search-works-hnsw-recall.description: Why exact nearest-neighbour search does not scale, how HNSW graphs and compressed IVF indexes find close-enough answers fast, and how to tune the recall you are quietly giving up.

verifying-code-you-did-not-write.title: Your Tests Were Never This Important: Verifying Code You Did Not Write
verifying-code-you-did-not-write.description: When generation is cheap, verification is the whole job. Property tests, mutation testing, and why passing your suite means less than it used to.

voice-ai-agents-latency-turn-taking-spee.title: Voice AI Agents: Latency, Turn-Taking and Speech-to-Speech Models
voice-ai-agents-latency-turn-taking-spee.description: A voice agent lives or dies on the half-second after the caller stops talking. How chained and speech-to-speech architectures compare, and how to engineer turn-taking that feels natural.

wearables-remote-monitoring-early-warnin.title: Wearables and Remote Monitoring: From Step Counts to Early Warning
wearables-remote-monitoring-early-warnin.description: Consumer watches now carry FDA-cleared alerts, and Medicare pays for remote monitoring. The evidence shows what an alert from the wrist is worth, and where the regulatory line sits.

weathernext-3-learns-from-observations-n.title: WeatherNext 3 Stopped Learning From Forecasts and Started Learning From the Sky
weathernext-3-learns-from-observations-n.description: Google DeepMind's model trains on live satellite mosaics and raw station readings instead of forecast output. That one change removes a six-hour lag.
